rule: In Quenya the vowel-sign sits over the PRECEDING consonant (Appendix E, The Tengwar). A vowel with no preceding consonant rides a carrier.

a.cite: Appendix E, The Tengwar: the a-tehta is the three-dot sign. [I-H] -- read off the plate, since Appendix E's tables are images in the edition this archive holds.

e.cite: Appendix E, The Tengwar: the e-tehta is the acute. [I-H] -- read off the plate.

i.cite: Amanyë Tenceli, The Classical Mode, citing Appendix E: long í 'is indicated by a doubled dot', so short i is the SINGLE dot. Confirmed against the font's own geometry -- see the note below.

o.cite: Appendix E, The Tengwar: o is a right curl, u a left. [I-H] -- read off the plate.

u.cite: Appendix E, The Tengwar: o is a right curl, u a left. [I-H] -- read off the plate.

owed: Correctness is NOT established until this is proven against Glaemscribe's published output. Until then this is a careful reading of Appendix E.
